title: The tempo you can hold
summary: Record yourself against a metronome and measure, honestly, how steady your beat really is.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A bar of eight steady clicks, a stretch of the metronome track the recording is checked against, counting how many of the first twenty beats landed exactly on the click.

steps.title: The tempo you can hold
steps.body:
It feels steady while you play. It often is not. This week the metronome and a recording tell the truth instead of your own sense of time. Your sense of time speeds up under pressure and slows down in the easy bars, without asking permission.

1. Record yourself playing the hard bar along with the metronome clicking underneath.
2. Listen back with the recording and the click together, and mark every beat where your note landed early or late.
3. Count how many of the first twenty beats landed exactly on the click, and write that number in the log.
4. Practise the same bar slowly with the click, aiming to raise that count next sitting.

A metronome does not care how the bar felt. It only reports what actually happened, and that is exactly why it is useful.

figure.alt: The same eight steady clicks, the track a new recording is checked against each sitting, aiming to raise the count of beats landed exactly on time.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: record the hard bar against the click, count beats exactly on time
Sitting 2: practise slowly with the click, then record and count again
Sitting 3: try a second hard bar the same way, count its beats
Sitting 4: the whole piece against the click, then once as if recording
An old piece played once with the metronome, just to listen

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Say the piece and your best count out of twenty, then play the hard bar once against the click, hands in the frame.

extras.title: A steadiness score for the whole piece
extras.body:
1. Play the whole piece once with the metronome clicking, and record it.
2. Split the piece into the same sections you have used before.
3. For each section, count how many beats landed exactly on the click, out of the first ten in that section.
4. Compare the sections: which one scores highest, which one scores lowest.

What to notice: the section that feels easiest is not always the one that is actually steadiest.
